findings.description: Gateway ReceiptMaintenance retains only one ExportLease. A preview in another tab overwrites the first live tab export identity, so its next chunk/rotate rejects archive_expired even though the core now retains both export snapshots. This defeats the implemented independent-tab export behavior.

A definitively rejected stop writes a nextStop cooldown. If turn/completed later finishes the run via the notification path, it deletes nextRead but not nextStop. The run leaves outstanding(), so that cooldown is never visited again; repeated affected runs grow the Map without retention bounds.

DiagnosticRedactor does not register HARNESS_PROVIDER_KEY_DEFAULT or HARNESS_PROVIDER_KEY_<32HEX> values, although configFromEnvironment explicitly supports those managed provider variables. A diagnostic/native error containing the configured credential as a bare value survives both text and structured redaction, unlike the legacy HARNESS_PROVIDER_API_KEY path.

After awaiting rpc.close() and its owned cleanup proof, the Linux launcher test probes rpc.processId using process.kill(pid, 0). A reused numeric PID can falsely fail an otherwise successful cleanup assertion. This particular call is signal 0 and does not kill an unrelated process.

prepare checks only the compact public view, then serializes private model instructions and native catalogs without enforcing the 4 MiB settings read limit. Two individually valid provider catalogs can therefore create a generation that read/verify refuses; activation stops services before this late failure. Profiles.save independently adds metadata around a valid near-limit settings object and can persist an oversized profile, after which Profiles.records/public and provider/read reject the retained profile.

Builder.toolchain reuses the fixed toolchain directory whenever its contents match the stored manifest, without binding that manifest to current Node/pnpm/Codex versions or distribution hashes. No control-update or application-update path refreshes this cache. An existing 0.164 installation therefore reuses 0.164 while preparing the 0.169 candidate, and the explicit runtime probe rejects it only after dependency fetch/install/build. Repeated attempts cannot self-correct and consume retained candidate slots. The final probe prevents publishing the old CLI; this is an upgrade blocker rather than a claim of silent successful downgrade.

Unsaved settings edits are guarded only by Settings Dialog.onClose. Internal project rename/remove, draft/history opening and native-terminal navigation invoke parent callbacks directly and can replace/unmount Settings with dirty provider/profile/extension/remote fields still present. The extension project selector also remounts its keyed child editors immediately, dropping unprepared skill/plugin/sharing edits without confirmation.

Current architecture and generated-protocol notice still claim 2.3.3/CLI 0.164.0. Architecture conversion also claims creation under source provider, whereas 0.169 compatibility requires target provider from creation. Update current contract only; retain explicitly historical evidence.

After awaiting the owned child/controller exit proof, the preflight checks and finally kills the old numeric child PID. PID reuse can both falsely fail verification and kill an unrelated process. Use bound controller/Job/exited proof and owned ChildProcess termination, never raw historical PID fallback.

note: The native test historical-PID finding and tooling preflight finding share a failure class but have separate affected paths. Scoped reports are complete at their declared inspection depth; aggregated explicit inspectedFiles omit 90 mostly runtime test/fixture files that were inventoried broadly. The next round must expand content and semantic review, not relabel that inventory as completed inspection. This round is not a clean audit or full-test authorization.
